schedules.pageSubtitle: Create and start tasks automatically on schedule. Two types: agent (dispatched to Claude Code) and shell (runs a command directly).
schedules.noMatchDesc: Try adjusting the filters or click reset
schedules.emptyDesc: Click "+ New schedule" in the top right to create one
schedules.noTaskTip: This run did not create a task
schedules.errExprRequired: Schedule expression is required (5-field cron or ISO time)
schedules.errTitleRequired: Task title is required (used for agent dispatch)
schedules.errPromptRequired: Prompt is required (used for agent dispatch)
schedules.descWarn: No description — harder to trace intent when investigating incidents
schedules.noTaskId: This run has no task_id, cannot navigate
schedules.hintCron: 5 fields: min hour day month weekday, e.g. 0 9 * * *
schedules.hintTitle: Title shown when the agent dispatches a task.
schedules.hintPrompt: Instruction the agent receives when dispatching a task (natural language).
schedules.hintExecLocked: Type cannot be changed when editing (the backend PATCH whitelist excludes exec_type).
schedules.deleteConfirmMsg: "{name}" will be deleted immediately and cannot be recovered (not soft-deleted). Its run history will be deleted too.

templates.pageSubtitle: Package your usual prompt + model/LLM config + max turns + effort + auto-approve into a template, then reuse with one click when creating tasks.
templates.emptyDesc: Create a template to package your usual prompt + config for one-click reuse when creating tasks
templates.hintModel: Leave empty for resolution-chain default; or pick a specific model.
templates.hintLlm: Pick "Default" to use the resolution chain; pick a specific config to use that one.
templates.errMaxTurns: Max turns must be a positive integer
templates.deleteConfirmMsg: "{name}" will be deleted immediately and cannot be recovered.

runners.errPortRange: port must be an integer between 1 and 65535
runners.copyFailed: Copy failed — select and copy manually
runners.pageSubtitle1: Remote execution daemon for whitelisted commands across machines. Each runner = one
runners.pageSubtitle2: process on a target machine, authenticating heartbeats with a 256-bit token. Start manually for now (no launchd / Windows service).
runners.roleHint: ⚠️ Current account is not admin — register/delete/health check will be rejected by the backend (HTTP 401).
runners.formWarning1: 🔴 The token is shown once in a dialog after registration — close it and it's gone. Copy it right away to configure on the target machine:
runners.formWarning2: Don't expose the port to the public internet; agents only run whitelisted commands, but the token is a shared secret — if it leaks, anyone can run whitelisted commands on that machine.
runners.adminOnlyDesc: The Runners page is admin-only — register/delete/health check are cross-user infrastructure actions. Sign in with an admin account.
runners.emptyDesc: Fill in the form above to register a target machine's daemon.
runners.tokenIntro1: One-time token for runner "{name}" — once you close this dialog it's gone. Write it into the target machine's
runners.tokenTip: 🔴 Closing this dialog loses the token forever — you would have to re-register.
runners.closeBtn: Close (token will no longer be visible)
runners.deleteConfirmMsg: Are you sure? Its token will be revoked and the configured daemon will get 401 on its next heartbeat. host:port ({host}:{port}) can be registered again later.
